Defenced
de-FENST
adjective
The Authorized Version’s form of defensed, from defence — Latin defendere, to ward off. A defenced city is a fortified city, walled and garrisoned; the word describes a place made strong against assault.

Biblical Definition

A defenced city is a fortified one, and Isaiah uses the word almost entirely to show such cities falling. “Thou hast made of a city an heap; of a defenced city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built” (Isa 25:2). And again, “the defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed” (Isa 27:10) — cattle grazing where walls stood. The historical instance is Sennacherib, who “came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them” (Isa 36:1); every fortress in the kingdom fell, and only Jerusalem was left, and Jerusalem was delivered by an angel rather than by masonry. God then says something remarkable to the Assyrian himself: “Hast thou not heard long ago, how I have done it; and of ancient times, that I have formed it? now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste defenced cities into ruinous heaps” (Isa 37:26). The conqueror was an instrument, and did not know it. Yet the same word is used once in the opposite direction, and it is one of the great promises to a frightened minister: “I have made thee this day a defenced city, and an iron pillar, and brasen walls against the whole land” (Jer 1:18). Cities of stone fall; God fortifies men.

Webster 1828 Definition

Fortified; walled and garrisoned against attack. Used in Isaiah chiefly of strong cities that nevertheless fell, and once of a prophet made strong by God.

expand to see more

DEFENCED, pp. Fortified; guarded; secured against attack.

The older form of defensed; from defence, Latin defendere, to ward off.

Of a city: surrounded with walls and works of defence (Isa 36:1).

DEFENCE, n. That which guards or protects; fortification; resistance.

Jer 1:18 applies the term figuratively to a man made strong by God.

Key Scripture

Isa 25:2 — "For thou hast made of a city an heap; of a defenced city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built."

Isa 36:1 — "Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them."

Isa 37:26 — "Hast thou not heard long ago, how I have done it; and of ancient times, that I have formed it? now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste defenced cities into ruinous heaps."

Jer 1:18 — "For, behold, I have made thee this day a defenced city, and an iron pillar, and brasen walls against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against the princes thereof, against the priests thereof, and against the people of the land."

Modern Corruption

Security is sought in structures — walls, systems, reserves, institutions — and Isaiah’s repeated point is that the defenced city is precisely the thing that falls.

expand to see more

The corruption is misplaced confidence in structures. Every generation builds what it takes to be unassailable — walls, treaties, reserves, institutions, retirement accounts, reputations — and each generation is surprised when they fail. Isaiah writes as if the surprise itself were the folly. He has watched the strongest cities of Judah taken one after another by Assyria, and he draws the conclusion that fortification is not the same as safety. The point is not that walls are wrong; Nehemiah built them and God approved. The point is that a wall is a means, and a means trusted as an end becomes an idol that will certainly disappoint its worshippers.

Recover the plain sense: Isa 37:26 supplies the sovereignty that makes sense of the ruins. Sennacherib imagined he was making history and was told he was executing a purpose formed of ancient times — now have I brought it to pass. Nothing fell by accident. And the promise of Jer 1:18 supplies the comfort, for it moves the fortification from the stone to the man. Jeremiah was a young man told he would face kings, princes, priests, and the people of the land, and God did not promise him a quiet ministry; He promised they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee. The city that survived Sennacherib survived by an angel, and the prophet who survived Judah survived because God made him a defenced city.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin defendere, to ward off — fortified; in Isaiah the cities that fell, and in Jeremiah the man God made strong.

expand to see more

Defenced — the AV form of defensed; Latin defendere, to ward off.

Of a city: walled, garrisoned, and provisioned against siege.

Isa 36:1: Sennacherib took all the defenced cities of Judah.

Isa 37:26: the conqueror was executing a purpose formed of ancient times.

Jer 1:18: God makes a man a defenced city, an iron pillar, and brasen walls.

Usage

"In Isaiah the defenced city is characteristically the thing that falls."

"Walls are a lawful means; a means trusted as an end becomes an idol."

"Jerusalem survived by an angel, not by masonry."
